arxiv-2205-02849.title: AdaTriplet: Adaptive Gradient Triplet Loss with Automatic Margin Learning for Forensic Medical Image Matching
arxiv-2205-02849.creator: Khanh Nguyen, Huy Hoang Nguyen ⋆, Aleksei Tiulpin
arxiv-2205-02849.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Khanh Nguyen, Huy Hoang Nguyen ⋆, Aleksei Tiulpin. This paper tackles the challenge of forensic medical image matching (FMIM) using deep neural networks (DNNs). FMIM is a particular case of content-based image retrieval (CBIR). The main challenge in FMIM compared to the general case of CBIR, is that the subject to whom a query image belongs may be affected by aging and progressive degenerative disorders, making it difficult to match data on a subject level.

arxiv-2312-01276.title: Toward best research practices in AI Psychology
arxiv-2312-01276.creator: Anna Ivanova
arxiv-2312-01276.description: Abstract Language models have become an essential part of the burgeoning field of AI Psychology. I discuss 14 methodological considerations that can help design more robust, generalizable studies evaluating the cognitive abilities of language-based AI systems, as well as to accurately interpret the results of these studies.

arxiv-2407-16578.title: In-Situ Spheroid Formation in Distant Submillimeter-Bright Galaxies
arxiv-2407-16578.creator: Qing-Hua Tan 1,2, Emanuele Daddi 2, Benjamin Magnelli 2, Camila A. Correa 2, Frédéric Bournaud 2, Sylvia Adscheid 3, Shao-Bo Zhang 1, David Elbaz 2, Carlos Gómez-Guijarro 2, Boris S. Kalita 4,5,6, Daizhong Liu 1, Zhaoxuan Liu 4,5,7, Jérôme Pety 8,9, Annagrazia Puglisi 10,11, Eva Schinnerer 12, John
arxiv-2407-16578.description: Abstract The majority of stars in today’s Universe reside within spheroids, which are bulges of spiral galaxies and elliptical galaxies [ 1 , 2 ] . Their formation is still an unsolved problem [ 3 , 4 , 5 ] .

arxiv-2507-14722.title: LeanTree: Accelerating White-Box Proof Search with Factorized States in Lean 4
arxiv-2507-14722.creator: Matěj Kripner, Michal Šustr, Milan Straka
arxiv-2507-14722.description: Abstract Automated theorem proving (ATP) has been a classical problem in artificial intelligence since its inception, yet it remains challenging due to its vast state and action space. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as a promising heuristic for ATP, but they lack correctness guarantees and thus require interaction with a proof verifier.

arxiv-2511-22087.title: SoftNash: Entropy-Regularized Nash Games for Non-Fighting Virtual Fixtures
arxiv-2511-22087.creator: 1 st Tai Inui, 2 nd Jee-Hwan Ryu
arxiv-2511-22087.description: Abstract Virtual fixtures (VFs) improve precision in teleoperation but often “fight” the user, inflating mental workload and eroding the sense of agency. We propose Soft-Nash Virtual Fixtures , a game-theoretic shared-control policy that softens the classic two-player linear-quadratic (LQ) Nash solution by inflating the fixture’s effort weight with a single, interpretable scalar parameter τ \tau .

arxiv-2512-03311.title: Singing a Maximal Independent Set
arxiv-2512-03311.creator: Sandy Irani, Michael Luby
arxiv-2512-03311.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sandy Irani, Michael Luby. We introduce a broadcast model called the singing model , where agents are oblivious of the size and structure of the communication network, even their immediate neighborhood. Agents can sing multiple notes which are heard by their neighbors. The model is a generalization of the beeping model [ 1 , 6 ] , where agents can only emit sound at a single frequency.

arxiv-2601-08155.title: Instance-Aligned Captions for Explainable Video Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2601-08155.creator: Inpyo Song, Minjun Joo, Joonhyung Kwon, Eunji Jeon, Jangwon Lee
arxiv-2601-08155.description: Abstract Explainable video anomaly detection (VAD) is crucial for safety-critical applications, yet even with recent progress, much of the research still lacks spatial grounding, making the explanations unverifiable. This limitation is especially pronounced in multi-entity interactions, where existing explainable VAD methods often produce incomplete or visually misaligned descriptions, reducing their trustworthiness.

europmc-pmc8689412.creator: Gan BH, Gaynord J, Rowe SM, Deingruber T, Spring DR.
europmc-pmc8689412.description: Bacterial infections caused by 'superbugs' are increasing globally, and conventional antibiotics are becoming less effective against these bacteria, such that we risk entering a post-antibiotic era. pmc-11586484.title: Imperatorin Suppresses Aberrant Hedgehog Pathway and Overcomes Smoothened Antagonist Resistance via STAT3 Inhibition
pmc-11586484.creator: Juan Wang, Hua Cheng, Xinyue Zhao, Xiuwen Zhang, Xiaolei Ding, Taomin Huang
pmc-11586484.description: BackgroundHyperactive Hedgehog (Hh) signaling initiates and drives the progression of various tumors. Despite the clinical success of Hh inhibitors targeting Smoothened (SMO), drug resistance, often stemming from SMO mutations, remains a formidable obstacle in cancer therapy. Here, we investigated the potential of imperatorin (IMP), a Chinese herbal medicine, to overcome drug resistance and revealed the potential mechanisms.

pmc-11634736.title: CASIN exerts anti‐aging effects through RPL4 on the skin of naturally aging mice
pmc-11634736.creator: Yijia Zhang, Xueer Wang, Jianyuan Huang, Xinyue Zhang, Lingwei Bu, Yarui Zhang, Fengting Liang, Shenhua Wu, Min Zhang, Lu Zhang, Lin Zhang
pmc-11634736.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Skin aging has been associated with the onset of various skin issues, and recent studies have identified an increase in Cdc42 activity in naturally aging mice. While previous literature has suggested that CASIN, a specific inhibitor of Cdc42 activity, may possess anti‐aging properties, its specific effects on the epidermis and dermis, as well as the underlying mechanisms in naturally aging mice, remain unclear.

pmc-12708740.title: Analysis of AQP4 SNPs and Their Association With REM Sleep Behavior Disorder and Hallucinations in Parkinson’s Disease
pmc-12708740.creator: Cristina Agliardi, Franca Rosa Guerini, Milena Zanzottera, Elisabetta Bolognesi, Mario Meloni, Francesca Lea Saibene, Roberta Zangaglia, Andrea Sturchio, Carlo Casali, Cherubino Di Lorenzo, Jorge Navarro, Brigida Minafra, Mario Clerici
pmc-12708740.description: The glymphatic system is a glial-dependent network responsible for the clearance of waste products from the brain through cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation. This process, which involves astrocytes and the water channel AQP4, facilitates the removal of harmful proteins like β-amyloid and tau, making it crucial in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD).

pmc-13124961.title: From organelles to therapy: rethinking combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma
pmc-13124961.creator: Tiezhong Zhang, Kangshuai Li, Qi Li, Qiang Gao, Lixin Du, Jian Deng, Zhuohan Cao, Sen Guo, Zongli Zhang
pmc-13124961.description: Combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC-CCA) is a rare primary malignant hepatic neoplasm, defined by the concurrent presence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) components, which vary in proportion and degree of differentiation. Characterized by insidious onset, high invasiveness, and marked heterogeneity, cHCC-CCA often eludes early diagnosis, leading to a generally dismal prognosis.

pmc-13458662.title: Differential reinforcement using matched examples and nonexamples expedites the practice needed to learn concepts
pmc-13458662.creator: Catherine L. Williams, Rebecca E. Woodard, Mackenzie R. Fowler, Brooke A. Franks‐Jacobucci
pmc-13458662.description: Conceptual learning refers to correctly identifying novel examples and nonexamples of a concept. Concepts can be taught by presenting stimuli and differentially reinforcing responses to examples but not nonexamples. However, it is unclear which stimuli should be used and whether specifically designed stimuli can result in correct responding even in the absence of differential reinforcement.
